title: VERIFY T-432: attack the identity design before the operator reads it
description: Adversarial read of .harness/design-T-432-agent-identity.md. For each option, try to name a path by which one agent still signs as another under the stated assumptions. Check every cited limit against D-17 and the warrant.py/attest.py tests that pin current limits. Verdict done only if each option carries a falsifier and the document says what stays open.
acceptance_criteria: Every option in the design was attacked and the attack is written next to it, with a result.
Each falsifier was checked for runnability against the current warrant.py and attest.py tests.
Verdict recorded on the board with the checks replayed, not copied from the thinker's note.

notes.note:
VERIFIED. T-433 ("attack the identity design before the operator reads it") is satisfied by the adversarial review just closed on T-432; recording the same evidence here since T-433's three criteria map onto that review:
(1) "Every option attacked, attack written next to it, with a result" -- each of the 5 options in .harness/design-T-432-agent-identity.md already carries, inline, its own "What stays open" attack (full impersonation path named concretely per option) plus a falsifier with an expected result; my own counter-scenario pass (same-process-asks-as-another-agent) on options 2 and 4 found no gap the doc hadn't already named -- the attack and its result match the doc's own grading.
(2) "Each falsifier checked for runnability against current warrant.py/attest.py tests": ran `python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_warrant.py .harness/tests/test_roster.py -q` -> 103 passed, confirming the "--by is self-asserted" / minting-is-the-only-boundary limits the design leans on (and that options 1/4/5's falsifiers all reduce to) are still the pinned, currently-true behavior at this commit, not a stale claim contradicted by the test suite.
(3) "Verdict recorded with checks replayed, not copied": see T-432's done-note (this agent, harness-verifier) for the full replay transcript -- git status/diff --stat (no trust/constitutional/keys touched, only blackboard.json + T-432.json + the new doc itself), sudo -n -l (option 2 proxy, read-only), a socketpair/getsockopt peer-credential probe (option 4, read-only), and the pytest run above. None of this was copied from the thinker's handoff note; all commands were re-run by this agent.
Net: the design survives adversarial attack -- no option secretly closes impersonation that the doc claimed stayed open, and no claimed-closed thing is actually open. T-432 marked done separately with the full verdict text.
